authoring: Single-author synthetic evaluation corpus; labels were not independently annotated.
relevanceRule: A candidate is relevant exactly when it has the same scenarioId as the source query, is a different incident, and is in the same split. Scenario IDs and this rule are metadata only and are never sent to PostgreSQL or included in incident text.

incident.title: Checkout API waits for a database connection
incident.description: Cart submissions pause before SQL work begins. Request traces show long acquisition waits and repeated pool saturation during the morning peak.
incident.rootCause: Connections leaked by abandoned checkout transactions exhausted the shared PostgreSQL pool.
incident.fixApplied: Closed connections on every rollback path and raised the pool ceiling after validating database capacity.

incident.title: Order placement stalls at connection checkout
incident.description: The web checkout remains responsive but database calls queue without starting. Pool metrics reach their limit while database CPU stays low.
incident.rootCause: A retry branch retained idle SQL sessions, leaving no free database connections for order workers.
incident.fixApplied: Released sessions after retries and added an alert for connection-pool utilization.

incident.title: Cart requests time out acquiring SQL sessions
incident.description: Checkout latency rises sharply; traces end at connection acquisition and show no slow query. PostgreSQL has spare CPU and active sessions are at the configured cap.
incident.rootCause: A missing finally cleanup in the cart transaction path caused gradual connection pool exhaustion.
incident.fixApplied: Added unconditional transaction cleanup, drained leaked sessions, and tuned the pool limit.

incident.title: Checkout database handoff blocks during traffic spikes
incident.description: Order API workers wait for an available connection even though database query execution is fast. The symptom is intermittent after retries.
incident.rootCause: Checkout retry handling failed to return pooled connections after an upstream request was cancelled.
incident.fixApplied: Returned connections on cancellation and added pool saturation telemetry.

incident.title: Checkout shows retired catalog prices
incident.description: The cart service serves old product amounts after catalog updates. Database latency and connection counts remain normal; cache entries outlive product revisions.
incident.rootCause: Redis catalog keys omitted the product revision, so invalidation missed older cached price records.
incident.fixApplied: Versioned catalog cache keys and invalidated stale entries during price publication.

incident.title: Cart totals use stale item cache after a price change
incident.description: Checkout calculations disagree with the product page for recently edited items. SQL reads are current but the cart cache continues returning previous values.
incident.rootCause: A cache invalidation event used the SKU while readers keyed entries by internal product id.
incident.fixApplied: Aligned cache identity on product id and replayed missed invalidation events.

incident.title: Catalog edits are not reflected in checkout baskets
incident.description: The checkout application reports outdated item metadata several minutes after successful catalog writes. The database is healthy and cache hit ratio is unusually high.
incident.rootCause: The catalog cache used a non-versioned key and refresh messages were dropped by a consumer restart.
incident.fixApplied: Added revision-aware cache keys and rebuilt entries from the current catalog.

incident.title: Checkout basket retains an old product amount
incident.description: Only recently changed products are affected. New sessions get correct prices; long-lived cart sessions reuse a cached catalog snapshot.
incident.rootCause: The basket service did not compare cached catalog revision with the latest published revision.
incident.fixApplied: Checked catalog revisions before applying cached prices and expired outdated basket snapshots.

incident.title: Payment gateway rejects TLS handshakes
incident.description: Card authorization calls fail before an HTTP response. Gateway connections report certificate validation errors after the provider endpoint rotated its leaf certificate.
incident.rootCause: The outbound payment trust bundle lacked the provider's new intermediate certificate.
incident.fixApplied: Installed the updated certificate chain and verified the gateway handshake from every region.

incident.title: Card authorizations fail certificate verification
incident.description: Payment requests terminate during TLS setup with an unknown issuer message. Application credentials and provider availability checks pass.
incident.rootCause: A renewed gateway certificate chained to an intermediate absent from the service trust store.
incident.fixApplied: Refreshed the CA bundle and restarted payment workers to load the new chain.

incident.title: Billing cannot establish a secure provider session
incident.description: The payment integration sees handshake alerts and no authorization identifiers. The failure began immediately after a certificate renewal.
incident.rootCause: The gateway rotated its signing chain but our pinned intermediate certificate had expired.
incident.fixApplied: Replaced the pinned intermediate with the provider's current chain and tested a live authorization.

incident.title: Provider certificate rotation breaks payment connections
incident.description: TLS clients in the billing service reject the remote certificate while browser checks succeed. The service uses a separately packaged trust bundle.
incident.rootCause: The container image bundled an outdated certificate authority chain for the payment gateway.
incident.fixApplied: Updated the container trust package and rolled out fresh payment instances.

incident.title: Payment authorizations receive provider throttling responses
incident.description: The gateway returns HTTP 429 for bursts of card requests while TLS and credentials remain valid. Retry traffic amplifies the queue during checkout peaks.
incident.rootCause: The payment account exceeded its per-second authorization quota after a traffic increase.
incident.fixApplied: Added bounded exponential backoff and negotiated a higher provider request quota.

incident.title: Card processing is delayed by upstream rate limits
incident.description: Payment API responses contain a rate-limit header and retry-after value. Gateway TLS checks pass and requests succeed when spaced out.
incident.rootCause: A new batch settlement job shared the interactive authorization quota with checkout traffic.
incident.fixApplied: Separated settlement and interactive limits and paced background requests.

incident.title: Billing gateway returns too many requests
incident.description: Authorization calls are rejected with 429 responses after a campaign launch. There are no handshake errors and provider credentials are accepted.
incident.rootCause: Client retries ignored the provider retry-after instruction and multiplied requests during a short outage.
incident.fixApplied: Honored retry-after, capped concurrent attempts, and added a circuit breaker.

incident.title: Checkout payments hit the processor request ceiling
incident.description: The provider dashboard shows valid sessions but rejects authorization bursts. Failures cluster around simultaneous order submissions.
incident.rootCause: Payment workers scaled beyond the processor account's configured concurrency allowance.
incident.fixApplied: Applied a shared concurrency limiter and coordinated a processor capacity increase.

incident.title: Login tokens expire immediately on some nodes
incident.description: Users are redirected to sign-in after successful authentication. JWT validation differs by application host and token timestamps appear to be in the future.
incident.rootCause: Clock drift on two identity nodes exceeded the token verifier's allowed clock skew.
incident.fixApplied: Restored NTP synchronization and added an alert for host clock offset.

incident.title: Sessions are rejected because token time is ahead
incident.description: Authentication succeeds but follow-up API requests fail JWT validation. The issue follows requests routed to a subset of login servers.
incident.rootCause: A virtual machine resumed with a stale system clock and issued tokens outside the accepted time window.
incident.fixApplied: Resynchronized host clocks and rejected readiness until time service is healthy.

incident.title: Identity service creates already-expired access tokens
incident.description: Newly issued sessions fail in downstream services with issued-at and expiration checks. Token signatures are valid and signing keys match.
incident.rootCause: The identity container used the host's unsynchronized clock, producing timestamps several minutes ahead.
incident.fixApplied: Enabled chrony time synchronization in the node pool and verified JWT clock claims.

incident.title: JWT validation fails after successful user sign-in
incident.description: Login responses return normally, but session checks reject tokens with a not-yet-valid claim. Failures correlate with one availability zone.
incident.rootCause: An identity host clock lagged behind the rest of the fleet after time synchronization was disabled.
incident.fixApplied: Re-enabled NTP and added a fleet-wide clock-skew health check.

incident.title: Login fails after identity signing-key rotation
incident.description: JWT signatures are invalid only on a subset of authentication workers. System time is synchronized and newly restarted processes validate tokens.
incident.rootCause: Long-lived identity workers retained an obsolete signing key in their in-memory key cache.
incident.fixApplied: Published cache invalidation on key rotation and restarted workers that missed the event.

incident.title: Authentication rejects tokens signed by the current key
incident.description: The identity provider rotates its signing key successfully, but some login nodes keep checking against a previous key set. Clock diagnostics are clean.
incident.rootCause: The JWKS refresh timer stopped after a transient cache-control parsing error.
incident.fixApplied: Corrected cache header handling and forced a key-set refresh across authentication nodes.

incident.title: New access tokens fail signature checks on warm servers
incident.description: Fresh identity instances accept the rotated credential while warm servers return invalid signature. No token expiry or clock-skew errors are present.
incident.rootCause: A local key cache was not invalidated when the signing-key identifier changed.
incident.fixApplied: Keyed the cache by key identifier and invalidated the previous signing material.

incident.title: Rotated identity keys are missing from token validators
incident.description: Authentication reports unknown key ids until a process restart. Issued-at values are valid and the key provider publishes the new set.
incident.rootCause: Validators cached the remote signing-key document beyond its rotation lifetime.
incident.fixApplied: Bounded JWKS cache lifetime and refreshed signing keys when a token references an unknown id.

incident.title: Release rollout rejects a mismatched image manifest
incident.description: Deployment agents download the artifact but fail verification before starting containers. Registry availability is normal and retries return identical bytes.
incident.rootCause: The build pipeline published a stale manifest digest after reusing a mutable release tag.
incident.fixApplied: Published immutable image digests and verified the manifest against the signed build record.

incident.title: Deployment checksum differs from the release artifact
incident.description: New application pods never become ready because the fetched package hash does not match release metadata. Registry pulls complete without throttling.
incident.rootCause: A packaging task overwrote the archive after the checksum file had been generated.
incident.fixApplied: Made release artifacts immutable between packaging and signing and rebuilt the affected version.

incident.title: Signed deployment bundle fails integrity verification
incident.description: The orchestrator refuses the rollout with a digest mismatch even though all artifact downloads succeed. The problem affects one release only.
incident.rootCause: The release manifest referenced the digest of an earlier container layer after a concurrent build reused the tag.
incident.fixApplied: Pinned each deployment manifest to a content-addressed artifact and regenerated its signature.

incident.title: Application rollout stops on corrupt package metadata
incident.description: Deployment workers retrieve the correct package size but the embedded digest is invalid. Network transfer metrics show no packet loss or retry storm.
incident.rootCause: A release metadata race paired a newly built archive with an old checksum record.
incident.fixApplied: Serialized metadata publication with artifact upload and reran the signed release.

incident.title: Deployment workers cannot pull images from registry
incident.description: Rollouts queue while image requests fail with authorization errors. The registry is reachable and package checksums are valid.
incident.rootCause: The deployment registry credential expired but node agents continued reusing the cached token.
incident.fixApplied: Rotated the registry pull secret and refreshed credentials on all deployment workers.

incident.title: Container image downloads stall during rollout
incident.description: Deployment nodes repeatedly retry image pulls and report registry throttling. Artifact signatures and digests validate when a pull completes.
incident.rootCause: A rollout wave exceeded the registry's concurrent download allowance.
incident.fixApplied: Limited parallel image pulls per node and staggered deployment waves.

incident.title: Release jobs receive registry rate-limit responses
incident.description: Build agents can authenticate but image layers return HTTP 429 during simultaneous deployments. No integrity or signing errors are observed.
incident.rootCause: Many deployment workers shared one registry account quota and exhausted its burst allowance.
incident.fixApplied: Added pull backoff and distributed deployment windows across the worker fleet.

incident.title: Image pull authentication fails on warm deployment nodes
incident.description: New nodes fetch release images but long-running agents receive unauthorized responses. Registry status is healthy and digests remain unchanged.
incident.rootCause: A node-local credential helper retained an expired registry token after secret rotation.
incident.fixApplied: Restarted credential helpers and made token refresh occur before each deployment window.

incident.title: Object uploads fail when storage volume runs out of inodes
incident.description: Small file writes return no-space errors despite free gigabytes on the disk. The filesystem reports inode exhaustion after temporary object fragments accumulated.
incident.rootCause: An upload retry loop created too many tiny staging files and delayed cleanup.
incident.fixApplied: Removed orphan fragments, bounded retries, and added inode utilization alerts.

incident.title: Storage rejects new objects with filesystem entry exhaustion
incident.description: Capacity dashboards show room for more bytes, but object creation fails with an inode limit error. Existing large objects remain readable.
incident.rootCause: The metadata volume accumulated excessive small temporary files from interrupted multipart uploads.
incident.fixApplied: Swept abandoned multipart entries and moved staging metadata to a larger-inode filesystem.

incident.title: Blob service cannot create files although disk space is free
incident.description: Storage writes report ENOSPC while byte-level disk consumption is below threshold. Filesystem inspection shows no available file nodes.
incident.rootCause: A cleanup regression left one directory entry per completed upload part.
incident.fixApplied: Repaired multipart cleanup and alerted on inode exhaustion independently from byte capacity.

incident.title: New object creation stops on a full inode table
incident.description: The storage cluster has substantial free capacity but cannot allocate filesystem entries. Reads and existing object retrieval continue to work.
incident.rootCause: Orphaned small object metadata consumed all inodes on the staging partition.
incident.fixApplied: Removed orphan metadata and moved temporary object records to a dedicated volume.

incident.title: Object reads return old metadata after a rename
incident.description: Storage clients can access the data but see an earlier object name and tag set. Disk capacity and filesystem entry counts are normal.
incident.rootCause: A metadata cache did not invalidate after the object rename transaction committed.
incident.fixApplied: Published rename invalidations after commit and versioned metadata cache entries.

incident.title: Storage listing omits recently moved blobs
incident.description: New object paths work directly but container listings preserve stale locations. Storage nodes have free capacity and healthy inode counts.
incident.rootCause: The listing index missed rename notifications delivered during a coordinator failover.
incident.fixApplied: Replayed the rename journal and made index consumers resume from durable offsets.

incident.title: Renamed objects retain previous tags in storage results
incident.description: Metadata updates are durable in the primary store but read replicas show old values after a path change. Volume utilization is ordinary.
incident.rootCause: Replica refresh skipped metadata rows whose object key changed during compaction.
incident.fixApplied: Rebuilt affected metadata replicas and applied key changes before compaction.

incident.title: Bucket search returns stale paths for moved objects
incident.description: Object retrieval at the new path succeeds while search and listings return the old name. The storage backend has no space or inode alerts.
incident.rootCause: A secondary metadata index consumed object updates before the rename transaction became visible.
incident.fixApplied: Reordered index consumption after commit and refreshed stale path entries.

incident.title: Queue consumers repeatedly retry one malformed message
incident.description: A single event is delivered to the same worker over and over, preventing later messages in its partition from progressing. Broker health is normal.
incident.rootCause: A poison payload failed schema decoding but the consumer did not move it to the dead-letter queue.
incident.fixApplied: Added schema quarantine and routed repeated decode failures to a bounded dead-letter topic.

incident.title: Event processing loops on an invalid queue record
incident.description: Consumer offsets stop advancing at one record while the message broker remains available. Restarting workers returns to the identical payload.
incident.rootCause: A malformed event was retried without a delivery limit because validation errors were treated as transient.
incident.fixApplied: Classified decode errors as permanent and sent the record to dead-letter storage for inspection.

incident.title: One poison event blocks progress in a message partition
incident.description: Queue depth rises behind a repeatedly failing event. Other partitions continue normally and broker replicas are healthy.
incident.rootCause: The consumer committed no offset for an unparseable payload and retried it indefinitely.
incident.fixApplied: Introduced a retry ceiling, dead-letter routing, and an operator replay workflow.

incident.title: Malformed notification prevents queue worker advancement
incident.description: A worker returns to the same notification after every restart and subsequent messages remain queued. No broker quorum or network alarms are active.
incident.rootCause: A payload encoding defect triggered an unbounded retry instead of message quarantine.
incident.fixApplied: Validated encoding before dispatch and quarantined invalid notifications after the first permanent failure.

incident.title: Queue backlog grows after a partition leader stops serving reads
incident.description: Consumers are healthy but cannot fetch from one message partition. The broker elects leaders repeatedly and replicated data remains intact.
incident.rootCause: An uneven partition assignment overloaded one broker until its leader heartbeat timed out.
incident.fixApplied: Rebalanced partition leaders and reduced per-broker assignment skew.

incident.title: Message consumers lag because broker fetches stall
incident.description: Queue records are valid and workers do not report decode retries. Fetch latency spikes on a broker with repeated leader changes.
incident.rootCause: A network path between consumers and the partition leader dropped large fetch responses.
incident.fixApplied: Corrected the broker route MTU and verified sustained fetch throughput.

incident.title: Consumer groups fall behind during broker re-election
incident.description: All queue messages are well-formed, but one broker repeatedly relinquishes partition leadership and clients pause consumption.
incident.rootCause: Disk latency delayed broker heartbeat processing beyond the configured session timeout.
incident.fixApplied: Moved the broker log to lower-latency storage and adjusted heartbeat scheduling.

incident.title: Partition consumers stop receiving records from the active leader
incident.description: Message production succeeds while consumer fetches time out on one shard. There are no poison-message indicators and other partitions progress.
incident.rootCause: A broker leader entered a network partition from its consumer-facing interface while replication continued.
incident.fixApplied: Restored consumer network reachability and added a fetch-path health probe.
